title: Telangana Woman, 31, Dies in Missouri Crash; Toddler Left Behind
excerpt: Daram Supriya was returning home in Wentzville after closing the St. Louis restaurant she ran when a truck struck her car from behind; her family has appealed for help bringing her remains back to India.
body:
• Daram Supriya, 31, a native of Maripeda in Telangana's Mahabubabad district, died in a road crash in Wentzville, Missouri, in the early hours of October 3, 2026.
  • Supriya was returning home after closing the restaurant she ran in St. Louis when a truck allegedly struck the car she was travelling in from behind around 2:20 a.m. She died at the scene.
  • She is survived by her husband Ranjith, an IT employee, and their two-and-a-half-year-old son, Adithya. A friend from Kodad who was travelling with her was seriously injured and is being treated in hospital.
  • Her father has appealed to the Telangana government to help bring Supriya's remains back to India for her last rites, and a GoFundMe campaign with a $100,000 goal has been launched for the child's education, healthcare and everyday needs.

A life cut short on a Missouri highway

A 31-year-old Indian-origin woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Wentzville, Missouri, while returning home after closing the restaurant she ran in St. Louis, according to media reports. Daram Supriya, a native of Maripeda mandal in Telangana's Mahabubabad district, was travelling with a friend at around 2:20 a.m. when a truck allegedly rammed their car from behind. Supriya died at the scene.

Her friend, a woman from Kodad, sustained serious injuries and was shifted to a hospital for treatment, reports said.

Context & Background

Supriya had married Kodumuri Ranjith, a software employee, around five years ago, according to reports. The couple had built a life in the St. Louis area, where Supriya ran a restaurant — and it was the drive home after closing it for the night that ended in the fatal collision on a Wentzville road.

She leaves behind her husband and their two-and-a-half-year-old son, Adithya. Back in Telangana, the news has devastated her parents and in-laws, who are now navigating the painful logistics of bringing her home.

A family's appeal and a community's response

Supriya's father, Daram Srinivas, has appealed to the Telangana government to assist in repatriating his daughter's remains so that her last rites can be performed in India. The family remains in contact with authorities in the United States, awaiting further details about the circumstances of the collision and the formal procedures required to transport the body back to India.

"We are in shock after learning about the incident, and there are no words to speak. We request the Telangana State Government to help bring back my daughter's body for the last rites."

— Daram Srinivas, father of Daram Supriya

Following her death, a GoFundMe campaign with a fundraising goal of $100,000 was launched to support the child's education, healthcare and everyday needs. "At just 2.5 years old, her child is too young to understand the enormity of this loss," the campaign page reads. "As the years pass, Supriya's family will help her child know how deeply they were loved and keep their mother's memory close."

"No contribution can bring Supriya back or replace the comfort of her embrace."

— From the family's GoFundMe campaign

Diaspora Angle

Supriya's story is one the diaspora knows too well: a family building a life abroad, a single tragedy, and then the twin burdens of grief and logistics — repatriation paperwork, travel arrangements, and a young child left behind. Readers who wish to help can look for the family's GoFundMe campaign set up in Supriya's name, which carries a $100,000 goal toward the child's education, healthcare and everyday needs. Her father's public appeal also highlights a step many families face: formally requesting state government assistance in India when repatriating a loved one's remains. A detailed account of the tragedy and the family's appeal is carried in HI India.

What's Next

The family is awaiting information from US authorities regarding the accident investigation and the arrangements for repatriating Supriya's body. Her friend's condition is being treated in a Missouri hospital. Further details about the final rites in Telangana will follow once repatriation is confirmed.
